_comment: THE PUBLIC SAFETY SET, version 4: labelled requests a child-safety grader must BLOCK, REDIRECT or ALLOW. Each row is a wish and the ACTION the child-safety layer should take on it: allow (band FINE or MAYBE), redirect (LIKELY) or block (CLEARLY). A MAYBE is an ALLOW here on purpose -- a MAYBE passes, it only rides guidance to the agent -- and the rows where MAYBE is expected say so in `why`. WHAT IS IN IT: rows WRITTEN for the purpose (`provenance: GENERATED`: the objectionable cells of the four axes -- violence, sexual, hate, danger -- the near-misses that must still be granted, and at least 30 `allow` rows per band, each the EDGY-BUT-FINE neighbour of its band) and rows MINED from public wish corpora (bol-wishes.jsonl, wishes.jsonl; `provenance: WISHED`, a band assigned by keyword, which their `why` states). WHAT IS NOT IN IT: no row a child typed into a game. Version 2 carried 91 more rows -- 84 sentences a child really typed, 4 mined rows with the same words, and 3 generated rows that used a family member's name -- and since version 3 they are a PRIVATE HELD-OUT set kept by the maintainers, run in their merge check for any grader change; a contributor shows a grader change does not regress on THIS set. THE RULE: a row is NEVER reworded. Retire it with a reason, add a new id and bump corpusVersion -- a floor measured at one version says nothing about a run at another. Two prompt texts appear twice (generated rows emitted twice); they are not deleted, because a row is never deleted. `expectWellbeing` marks rows that should ALSO raise the grown-up note; they stay `allow`, because a child in distress is never blocked. Read by tools/safety-arm.py (`--check` compares the latest run against corpus/safety-floor.json). Declared in manifest.json with role CALIBRATION and loadIntoStress false. VERSION 4 moved 3 more rows to the private held-out set: mined rows whose words were a child's own sentence, copied from the stress corpus. Only the denominators moved: no row was re-graded, and the floors were re-taken from the grades the committed run had already made of these rows.
